title: Graceful SSE reconnects with opaque chunk inspector and function-call alignment
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Clients experience partial or duplicated function-call events when Server-Sent Event (SSE) streams disconnect mid-chunk. Existing resume tokens are tied to JSONL boundaries and assume client can parse full events, which breaks across proxies and non-JSON consumers. Goal: Implement a robust SSE reconnect strategy that preserves tool/function-call atomicity, allows opaque proxies to validate and reassemble chunks, and minimizes duplicate tool invocations. Deliverables: 1) A chunk framing format that attaches a short opaque header to each SSE data fragment (fields: chunk_id, seq_offset, checksum, resume_hint) while keeping data body unchanged; 2) A lease-based resume token and resume negotiation protocol that supports weakly-consistent reconnects (client provides last-ack chunk_id + offset, server responds with reconciliation window and optional replaying of missing fragments); 3) Formal alignment rules for tool/function-call frames so a function-call is only considered delivered when its terminal chunk has been acknowledged; 4) SDK compatibility shims for Node/Python clients to expose an opt-in "guaranteed-tool-calls" mode and a diagnostic "opaque-chunk-inspector" helper for proxies; 5) End-to-end tests, performance benchmarks, and docs. Acceptance criteria: - No accidental double-invocation of function tools in 99.99% of simulated reconnect scenarios across 50k synthetic sessions; - Resume latency added < 2ms p95 for typical reconnect path; - Chunk header overhead <= 24 bytes; - SDKs expose the new resume handshake and a migration guide; - Confluence design doc and runtime-1.20 release notes updated.
comments: 2026-03-05 — Spike completed: verified existing resume-token semantics fail when SSE fragments split inside a function-call JSON envelope. Notes attached to Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SSE+Reconnect+Design

2026-03-06 — Design review with PM/DS/Infra. Decided to prefer an opaque chunk header (binary-safe base64 in HTTP header-like line) to avoid forcing JSON parsing on intermediaries. Feedback: make header compact and extensible.

2026-03-07 — Prototype implemented in runtime branch: feature/sse-opaque-chunk. Demonstrated resume negotiation with lease windows. Small demo video and trace: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1-demo-sse-resume

2026-03-08 — Security review request filed (ticket SEC-2047). Preliminary response: chunk headers must not leak PII and resume tokens must be short-lived and HMAC-signed. Follow-up: integrate KMS signing for resume tokens.

2026-03-09 — Integration tests with function-caller shim: added atomic commit marker (chunk flag FINAL_CALL) so SDKs can defer function invocation until final fragment ack. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345

2026-03-10 — Load test (k6) across 10k concurrent streaming sessions. Observation: minimal CPU overhead, small increase in network packets due to extra header; memory stable. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/sse-reconnect-loadtests?view=run-2026-03-10

2026-03-11 — UX/SDK sync: Node SDK will expose on('chunk-inspect') hook and Python will expose enable_guaranteed_tool_calls flag. Documented migration patterns in docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789

2026-03-12 — Code review feedback applied: shortened resume token, added server-side backoff hints, and updated tests to introduce intermittent proxy layer. Next: finalize rollout plan and prepare canary in runtime-1.20.
Future — QA checklist: flaky reconnection scenarios, long-tail partial chunk arrival, cross-region reconnects, validation of HMAC expiry behavior, e2e demo for Solutions Engineering.
